title: Long TLT — Qatar-Egypt-Pakistan Ceasefire Text Submitted; Oil-to-CPI-to-Rate-Relief Chain if Accepted
entry: Long TLT $82–$86 at the July 21 open or intraday. The Qatar-Egypt-Pakistan mediator coalition formally submitted a 10-day ceasefire proposal to both the United States and Iran on July 21, 2026 (Axios, Pravda USA, New Arab). The proposal would halt hostilities and reopen both Hormuz shipping lanes (southern route through Omani waters, northern route through Iranian waters) during the ceasefire window. TLT at $83.83 (July 20 close) reflects the current STEP ASIDE regime: 30Y at 5.03%, September hike probability at 48.7%, Brent at $88.01. Do NOT initiate above $87 — above that level the rate relief from Hormuz reopening may already be partially priced. The TBT long (long-tbt-warsh-sintra-july-hike-2026-07-02, expires July 25) is the existing opposing position; TLT long can coexist for 4 days. If ceasefire is confirmed before July 25: exit TBT immediately, double the TLT position.
stop_loss: $79.50 daily close (~5.2% below $83.83 reference) — at $79.50, either (1) the ceasefire proposal has collapsed publicly (Trump or Iran explicitly rejected it, restarting strikes) and Brent has re-spiked above $92, reversing the oil-to-CPI relief chain; or (2) the July 28–29 FOMC surprised materially more hawkish than the market expected, with Warsh signaling September hike above 70% probability and 30Y yields breaking above 5.25%. At $79.50, the rate relief thesis is broken and TLT has further downside toward prior cycle lows.
targets: $88 — Ceasefire accepted by both parties; Brent falls from $88 toward $74 on Hormuz reopening confirmation; 30Y falls from 5.03% toward 4.70%; September hike probability falls from 48.7% to below 25%; TLT gains +5% from $83.83; cover 40% of position

$93 — August CPI (August 12) prints below 2.9% YoY on energy disinflation from Hormuz reopening and 3-week oil price decline; sell-side resets September hike probability to sub-15%; 30Y yield falls toward 4.35%; TLT gains +11% from $83.83; cover 40% of remaining position

$98 — Full disinflation confirmation: FOMC July 28–29 statement removes explicit 'rate hike if needed' language; WTI sustains below $72 for 2 consecutive weeks after ceasefire; August CPI 2.7% or below; 30Y yield below 4.10%; TLT gains +17% from $83.83; hold final 20%
risk_reward: 1:3.3 to Target 3 from $83.83 reference (risk $4.33; T3 reward $14.17)
catalyst: On July 21, 2026, Qatar, Egypt, Pakistan, and additional regional mediators formally submitted a written 10-day ceasefire proposal to both the United States and Iran. The proposal is the first formal written text presented to both parties since the conflict escalated on July 7-9. Key terms: halt to all hostilities, full reopening of Hormuz shipping lanes within 24 hours of acceptance, and a 10-day negotiation window for a longer-term Hormuz transit arrangement. Neither Trump nor Iran has accepted as of July 21, but the formal submission is qualitatively different from prior informal back-channel overtures — it creates a structured decision point that both parties must respond to, reducing ambiguity. If accepted: Brent falls from $88.01 toward $72–$74 (pre-escalation levels) within 3–5 days. This would reduce August CPI by approximately 0.3–0.5 percentage points year-over-year on energy base effects, reducing September hike probability from 48.7% to below 25% and driving 30Y yields from 5.03% toward 4.60%–4.70%.
thesis:
The TLT long here is a structural hedge against the dominant book risk — the STEP ASIDE regime is maintained primarily because of WTI $82.29 and 30Y at 5.03%, both of which derive from the Iran/Hormuz escalation. If the escalation abates, the STEP ASIDE triggers decompress, and TLT is the direct beneficiary through the oil-to-CPI-to-rate channel. This is not a macro forecast; it is an event-driven optionality trade structured so that the maximum loss (5.2% stop from reference) is explicitly defined and small.

The oil-to-rate transmission is the mechanism: Brent at $88.01 adds approximately 0.8–1.0 percentage points to headline CPI on a year-over-year basis compared to a scenario where Brent is at $72. With Brent at $88, August 12 CPI is likely to print 3.2%–3.5%. With Brent at $72 (ceasefire scenario), August 12 CPI prints 2.7%–2.9%. The difference is approximately 50bps of CPI — enough to flip the September FOMC from 'hike likely' (current 48.7%) to 'skip confirmed' (below 25%). That shift in September pricing would drive 30Y yields 30–50bps lower, and TLT responds approximately 3–5% to every 30bps of 30Y yield decline.

The existing TBT long (opposing rate trade) is not a contradiction; it expires July 25 and reflects the WARSH/hawkish FOMC baseline. TLT long at $83.83 is the ceasefire optionality overlay that hedges the book. If the ceasefire happens before July 25 (4 days): exit TBT at market and double TLT. If no ceasefire by July 25: TBT expires, TLT becomes a clean standalone position into the FOMC (July 28–29). The FOMC is the terminal catalyst — Warsh's July 29 statement either confirms hawkishness (TLT falls toward $81–$82, close to stop) or surprises dovish on ceasefire energy disinflation (TLT rallies toward $88+).

The counter-party is the rate bear who argues: (1) 30Y at 5.03% is driven by fiscal supply ($36T debt, 6% of GDP deficit) and NOT by oil/Iran — ceasefire would not substantially move the 30Y even if it happened; (2) FOMC under Warsh is committed to 5%+ long end as an anti-deficit anchor and will not ease guidance even on energy disinflation; (3) the ceasefire proposal has been rejected by both parties implicitly (Axios notes 'neither Trump nor Iran has accepted' and 'both sides are determined to improve leverage'). These arguments support the small position size (3%) and tight stop ($79.50).
bull_case: Trump administration accepts the 10-day ceasefire by July 23. Iran follows within 24 hours. Hormuz southern route reopens July 24. Brent falls from $88 to $76 by July 25. 30Y closes at 4.78% by July 25 (30bps decline from 5.03%). TLT rallies from $83.83 to $87.50 by July 25. TBT long stops out at expiry profitably (separately). TLT reaches $88 (T1) by July 28 — the day before FOMC. Exit 40% at T1.
bear_case: Both parties reject the ceasefire proposal by July 24. US conducts additional strike on Iranian military infrastructure July 25. Brent re-spikes toward $93. 30Y holds above 5.10%. Warsh July 29 FOMC statement reiterates September hike as 'live option.' TLT falls from $83.83 toward $81–$79.50. Exit at $79.50 stop. Loss is -5.2% on a 3% position = 16bps total portfolio drag.
invalidation: $79.50 TLT daily close; OR both US and Iran explicitly reject the Qatar-Egypt-Pakistan ceasefire proposal and resume offensive operations (escalation confirmed rather than paused); OR July 28–29 FOMC statement explicitly upgrades September hike probability above 70% (Warsh removes 'data dependent' language in favor of explicit forward guidance for hike); OR July CPI (July 11 print for June data) comes in above 3.8% YoY (energy spike is structural rather than transient); OR 30Y yield breaks above 5.30% on two consecutive daily closes (supply/fiscal pressure overwhelming ceasefire relief scenario)
